name: Early Access Video Game
tagline: Small studio, loud community, little money
scope: A co-op survival game in early access: game mechanics, content, updates, community and marketing. Players already own the game and let you know every week what they like.
approachText: Extreme uncertainty: only numbers and reviews show what players enjoy. Money drains every sprint, and only traction brings more. The whole project runs agile: short iterations, experiments, player data and a willingness to pivot.
intro: You run a small game studio. The game is in early access, players are already playing it, and the money barely lasts a few months. Every sprint costs money – only features players truly enjoy pay off.

workstreams.name: Game mechanics
workstreams.why: Whether the game is fun only shows when people play it. Prototype, playtest, tweak.

workstreams.name: New maps and content
workstreams.why: Content ships with updates, and direction follows what players play most.

workstreams.name: Game economy and balance
workstreams.why: Tuned from data on thousands of matches, not from a spreadsheet up front.

workstreams.name: Servers and stability
workstreams.why: Continuous deployment and quick fixes for whatever crashes – a smooth flow of work.

workstreams.name: Community and Discord
workstreams.why: Talking to players means reacting to whatever is happening right now.

workstreams.name: Localization into six languages
workstreams.why: Careful, it sounds like a plannable job – but texts change with every update. Translation runs continuously, in batches.

workstreams.name: Streamer partnerships
workstreams.why: Only the numbers show what works. Short experiments and evaluation.

workstreams.name: Music and sound effects
workstreams.why: Sound is tuned through playtests, not by a spec.

discoveries.name: In-team voice chat
discoveries.why: After co-op missions, players want to talk to each other right in the game.

discoveries.name: Community mod workshop
discoveries.why: Modders spoke up as soon as the tools came out: they want a place to share mods.

milestones.name: Positive reviews
milestones.okText: Reviews are improving, players keep coming back.
milestones.lateText: Reviews are mixed, players are leaving.

milestones.name: Major update
milestones.okText: The major update brought back old players and new ones too.
milestones.lateText: The major update sank without a trace.

milestones.name: Version 1.0
milestones.lateText: Version 1.0 is out, but players aren't excited.

shift.title: The market flipped
shift.text: A big rival game focused on PvP combat came out, and the PvP players moved over. Your community now mostly wants co-op and mods – and says so loudly. Revealed factor: a loud player community.
shift.lesson: When the market flips, reordering the backlog isn't enough – the team has to test new assumptions fast. Hypotheses and experiments become the key practice.

gate.title: Publisher meeting
gate.text: The publisher decides whether to fund more months of development. What do you show?
gate.lesson: Funding decisions in an agile project rest on data: how many people play, how many come back, and what the team has learned.

choices.text: Player data, what we've learned and a playable new build
choices.feedback: The publisher added funding for three more months.

choices.text: A trailer and big plans for 1.0
choices.feedback: “And how many people play it today?” The publisher tied the money to results.

choices.text: Postpone the meeting until there's something to show
choices.feedback: Meanwhile, the publisher paused payments.

events.title: Wave of negative reviews
events.text: Players are posting negative reviews over crashes. The rating is dropping.
events.lesson: Stability is the foundation of value. Players forgive thin content, not a game that crashes.

choices.text: Spend a whole sprint on stability and tell the community openly
choices.feedback: Players appreciate the honesty. Fewer crashes.

choices.text: Ignore the crashes and ship new content
choices.feedback: New content shipped. The crashes stayed.

choices.text: Split the team in half
choices.feedback: Some fixes, some content. Nothing done properly.

events.title: Offer from a streamer
events.text: A big streamer offers to showcase the game – in exchange for exclusive content.
events.lesson: Promising dates for content that doesn't exist yet is dangerous in an agile project. Offer what you have.

choices.text: Offer early access to the new update, with no date promised
choices.feedback: The stream brought in hundreds of new players.

choices.text: Promise an exclusive map within two weeks
choices.feedback: The streamer is hyped. The team doesn't know about the map yet.

choices.text: Pay for a sponsored collab
choices.feedback: It works, but it's pricey.

events.title: Money for a battle pass
events.text: The publisher offers extra money if you add a battle pass by the end of the month.
events.lesson: When money and community trust are at stake, test the hypothesis before you commit.

choices.text: Gauge interest with a poll and a small test, then decide
choices.feedback: The poll was clear: the community doesn't want a battle pass. The item's value is now verified.

choices.text: Accept and add the battle pass
choices.feedback: The money came in. The community is frowning.

choices.text: Decline
choices.feedback: The publisher is disappointed, but the community is none the wiser.

events.title: Crunch before the update
events.text: A major update is coming and the team proposes a month of crunch – working nights.
events.lesson: Crunch boosts output short term and burns people out long term. A sustainable pace and smaller scope are cheaper.

choices.text: Cut the update's scope and keep a sustainable pace
choices.feedback: The update is smaller, but the team is OK.

choices.text: Go into crunch
choices.feedback: The update will be big. The team is exhausted.

choices.text: Delay the update by a week
choices.feedback: Players wait longer, the team can breathe.

events.title: Cheaters
events.text: Cheats are spreading through the game. Honest players are furious.
events.lesson: A problem that ruins the experience for all players comes before new features.

choices.text: A quick anti-cheat fix and open communication with players
choices.feedback: Fewer cheaters, a calmer community.

choices.text: Leave it until 1.0
choices.feedback: Meanwhile, the cheaters are having a blast.

choices.text: Ban manually
choices.feedback: It helps, but the team spends hours reading reports.

events.title: Popular mod
events.text: A community modder made a mod that more people play than some official maps. They want official support.
events.lesson: The community can be your best source of value. Test the interest and give it room.

choices.text: Collaborate and test interest in mod support
choices.feedback: Interest is huge. The value of mod support is now verified.

choices.text: Ban mods – they ruin our vision
choices.feedback: The modder leaves, and thousands of players with them.

choices.text: Hire them onto the team
choices.feedback: One more skilled person, but the community got no more openness out of it.

lavina.title: “Mostly Negative” rating
lavina.text: The game's rating dropped to “Mostly Negative”. Sales are tanking.
lavina.lesson: Ignored quality comes back the moment everyone can see it. Fixing it now costs more than two sprints ago.
lavina.unresolvedText: Bad reviews over crashes followed the game into version 1.0.

choices.text: A fix sprint, an apology and a gift for players
choices.feedback: Players accepted the apology. The rating is slowly recovering.

choices.text: Delete critical posts on Discord
choices.feedback: Screenshots of the deleted posts went viral.

choices.text: Run a sale
choices.feedback: New players came – and wrote more negative reviews.

mapa.title: Where's the promised map?
mapa.text: The streamer asks live where the promised exclusive map is. The team didn't make it in time.
mapa.lesson: A deadline promised without the team is a debt the team pays off. Honesty is cheaper than a half-finished job.
mapa.unresolvedText: The streamer kept griping about the broken promise for ages.

choices.text: Admit the slip and show the work-in-progress map live
choices.feedback: Viewers loved the behind-the-scenes look.

choices.text: Release the unfinished map
choices.feedback: The map is full of bugs and the streamer laughs at them the whole time.

choices.text: Weekend overtime
choices.feedback: The map is done. So is the team.

bojkot.title: Community boycotts the battle pass
bojkot.text: The community is boycotting the battle pass and review-bombing the game.
bojkot.lesson: An untested hypothesis gets paid for in lost trust. Trust comes back slower than money.
bojkot.unresolvedText: Players still remember the battle pass fiasco.

choices.text: Scrap the battle pass and refund players
choices.feedback: Painful, but the community appreciated it.

choices.text: Stick with it
choices.feedback: Reviews keep falling.

choices.text: Make it free
choices.feedback: The storm died down; the publisher's money is gone.

odchody.title: Devs quit after the crunch
odchody.text: Two experienced developers handed in their notice after the crunch.
odchody.lesson: Crunch takes its toll with a delay. Losing people costs more than an update a week late.
odchody.unresolvedText: More people left after release; the studio is weakened.

choices.text: Redistribute work, shrink the plan and hire juniors with mentoring
choices.feedback: A slower start, but the team stabilizes.

choices.text: More crunch so we make it
choices.feedback: More resignations on the desk.

choices.text: Freeze new features
choices.feedback: Players get nothing new.

exodus.title: Honest players are leaving
exodus.text: There are so many cheaters that honest players are leaving for the competition en masse.
exodus.lesson: A problem that ruins the experience won't wait for 1.0.
exodus.unresolvedText: The “game full of cheaters” reputation followed it into version 1.0.

choices.text: Anti-cheat right now, plus amnesty for players who come back
choices.feedback: Some players came back.

choices.text: Claim the problem is overblown
choices.feedback: The community sees it differently.

choices.text: Shut down the PvP servers
choices.feedback: Cheaters have nowhere to play. Neither do honest players.

mody_bonus.title: Mods bring in players
mody_bonus.text: Community mods are bringing in new players. Modders ask whether there could be a contest.
mody_bonus.lesson: Openness to the community is an investment that pays back – players create value themselves.
mody_bonus.unresolvedText: The modding community keeps the game alive even after version 1.0.

choices.text: Run a best-mod contest with a prize
choices.feedback: The contest brought dozens of mods and a wave of new players.

choices.text: Sell the best mods as paid content
choices.feedback: Modders feel robbed.

choices.text: Say thanks and leave it there
choices.feedback: A somewhat missed opportunity.
